rows.grounds: instrumental dual of pathin, denoting two channels or ways
instrumental dual of ūru, denoting the pair of thighs
compound: nakha+nail, kusuma+flower, śākhā+branch; instrumental plural describing toe-nails as flowering branches
past passive participle of ud-i, indicating emergence or appearance

items.question: Through which limb-paths and nail-flower branches is the embodied form manifested as risen?
premises: The two paths and two thighs function as instrumental channels.
The nail-flower branches adorn these bodily limbs.
An emergent state is expressed through these adorned features.
items.inference: The embodied form is manifested as risen through the adorned paths and thighs.
uncertainties: The precise referent of pathibhyām in this bodily imagery is contextually ambiguous.
items.plain_english: Through the two paths and the two thighs, adorned with nail-flower branches, it has risen forth.
